I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My father did it, his father did it. I know one thing: wheat in the autumn, corn in the summer. That is what this land is for. That is what everyone here grows. I do not need to think hard about this.

I have about 5 mu. Not more — I am 71, my knees ache, and I cannot manage more land alone anymore. My son moved to the city years ago. I will hire a neighbor with a tractor to plough for me and to help at harvest. I cannot do that work myself now.

For wheat, I will plough in October before planting. I buy my wheat seed from the village supply shop — the same improved variety I have used for many years. I do not trust new things I do not know. I will put down diammonium phosphate and urea as base fertilizer before planting, the same amounts I always use. I will irrigate three times: once in winter when it is dry, once when the stalks are rising, once when the heads are forming. I will spray twice — once for weeds in early spring, once for rust and aphids near heading. I expect to get maybe 380 jin per mu. Enough to sell some and keep flour for the year.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn immediately on the same fields. I buy hybrid corn seed — that is all they sell at the shop now, has been for thirty years. Corn does not need as much from me. The summer rains help. I irrigate twice if the rain is not enough. I spray herbicide once right after planting, that is usually enough. I use rotary tillage — lighter work than deep ploughing. I expect 500 jin per mu.

I am not trying to get rich. I just want the land to produce what it always has.
